faq.answer: Within the US, decline rental CDW/liability coverage offered by rental agency; company policy covers it.
Weekly/multi-day pass is reimbursable when economically equivalent to or cheaper than individual fares.

rules.source_quote: Rideshare services (Uber, Lyft) are reimbursable for business travel between airports, hotels, and work sites.
Taxis are reimbursable at metered fare plus reasonable tip (up to 20% of fare).
Tips for ground transportation are reimbursable up to 20% of the fare.
Rental cars are appropriate where rideshare/taxi is impractical (multiple stops/days, rural destinations, multiple-passenger transport).
Compact/mid-size default; full-size only for 3+ passengers/equipment; premium/luxury/SUV require manager approval.
Within the U.S., decline rental CDW/liability insurance offered by rental company.
Outside the U.S., accept rental company's CDW.
Pre-paid fuel and rental-company refueling charges are not reimbursable.
Personal vehicle mileage reimbursed at IRS standard rate ($0.67/mile for 2025).
Commuting mileage (home to regular office) is not reimbursable.
Mileage must include start, destination, business purpose, and miles.
Public transit is reimbursable at actual cost.
Multi-day/weekly transit passes are reimbursable when equivalent to or cheaper than individual fares.
Parking at business destinations, hotels, and airports is reimbursable at actual cost.
Long-term airport parking should be used for trips of 3+ days when cheaper than alternatives.
Valet reimbursable only when sole option or price difference vs self-parking is under $15.
Highway tolls incurred during business travel are reimbursable at actual cost.
SUV categories are not reimbursable unless required by terrain or capacity, with manager approval.
